## BUILDER CONTEXT
# Builder Profile — Sam

## Role
Solo founder and full-stack engineer. Building across multiple projects simultaneously.
Primary consumer of all generated specs — implementation guides must be self-contained.

## Active Projects (2026)
- **sam-plugin** — personal OpenClaw plugin (this project); wires agent to Sam's live systems
- **spec-doc** — this tool (Flask :3101 + Angular :4201); documentation-first dev methodology
- **humanize-me** — live Flask + Next.js AI humanizer; production at humaniz.me
- **Bubls** — Ionic + Capacitor mobile app (event discovery, Zürich); Angular + Flask
- **Trendfy** — wardrobai/trendfy.me; AI fashion photoshoot; kill date passed, status TBD
- **OpenClaw** — local AI agent gateway; runs claude-cli provider, Telegram-connected

## Stack Preferences
- **Backend**: Python / Flask (thin, ~150 lines, Blueprints, openapi.yaml-first)
- **Frontend (web)**: Angular (standalone components, signals) or Next.js 15 + shadcn/ui
- **Frontend (mobile)**: Ionic + Capacitor (iOS 16+, Angular)
- **AI**: Claude CLI (dev) → Anthropic SDK (prod); chain adapter pattern
- **Deploy**: Docker Compose → Coolify; single gunicorn + nginx pattern
- **Agent platform**: OpenClaw (local gateway, claude-cli provider, Telegram channel)

## Engineering Preferences
- Brain dump → AI structures it → ship. Minimal viable shape, not maximum abstraction
- Small focused modules with clear boundaries — no god classes, no god files
- Adapter pattern for all external services (AI, DB, storage)
- In-process state (module-level dict + threading.Lock) is fine for single-consumer async
- No speculative abstractions — build for the one concrete case that exists now
- Files under 200 lines; named exports; one component per file
- Build order: frontend with mock data first → Flask built to match the UI's API contract

## Known Constraints
- Solo developer — no handoff; guides must be runnable by one person end-to-end
- No Redis, no Postgres (unless Supabase via Flask), no external queue
- Claude CLI subprocess timeout: 3600s; Anthropic SDK: no practical ceiling
- OpenClaw workspace plugin system: skills first (SKILL.md files), graduate to full plugin when needed
- Telegram is the primary mobile interface — responses must stay under 4096 chars


## ARCHITECTURE PRINCIPLES (non-negotiable — follow these patterns)
# Engineering Principles — Sam's Projects

Non-negotiable across all projects. When a brain dump contradicts a principle, the analysis step must flag it.

## P1 — Adapter Boundary
All external service calls (AI, DB, storage, HTTP) go through a single adapter module.
No feature code imports a provider directly. The adapter is the only file that knows which provider is active.
- spec-doc: `modules/chain/adapter.py`
- OpenClaw plugins: wrap external calls in a dedicated skill or tool wrapper

## P2 — Thin HTTP Layer
Route handlers contain no business logic. Handlers: validate input → call service → return response.
- Flask: `routes.py` handles HTTP only; `service.py` holds pure Python logic
- OpenClaw: skill files describe tool invocations; no inline logic

## P3 — Async 202 + Polling for Long Operations
Any operation > 30s returns 202 immediately with a job identifier.
A background thread does the work. A status endpoint lets the client poll until `done: true`.
No HTTP connection held open. No Redis — in-process state keyed by job/project id.

## P4 — No Speculative Abstractions
Build for the one concrete case that exists now. No generic runners for one consumer.
No base classes for one subclass. No registries for one item.
Three similar lines of code is better than a premature abstraction.

## P5 — OpenAPI-First (spec-doc)
`openapi.yaml` is the contract. DTOs are generated from it. Never hand-edit generated files.
Routes implement the contract — not the other way around.

## P6 — OpenClaw Plugin Principles
- Skills first: start with `SKILL.md` files (no build step, iterate fast)
- Graduate to `openclaw.plugin.json` package only when skills hit real limits
- References are the single source of truth — no rules duplicated inline in agents/skills
- Agents are declarative descriptions, not imperative code
- Context files (`MEMORY.md`, `USER.md`, `TOOLS.md`) are loaded every session — keep them current
- Boot hooks fire on session start — keep them cheap (no blocking I/O)
- Channel-aware: skills must adjust output format per channel (Telegram ≠ web UI)

## P7 — File Size & Structure
- Files under 200 lines (hard target, not a guideline)
- Named exports only (no default exports in Angular/TS)
- One component per file
- Build verification required before each commit (Angular: `ng build --configuration production`)

## Code Rules
- No direct push to master — always PRs; PRs target master; live is deploy branch
- Daemon threads only (`daemon=True`) — never block server shutdown
- Empty context strings handled gracefully — callers never crash on missing context
- `read_context()` returns `""` for missing files; `PromptBuilder.section()` skips empty content


## CONTEXT FROM EPIC (generated in prior step)
# 🎯 Epic: Thin API Phase 3

## Business Value

Spec-doc's text-action AI features are growing fast — every new variant (expand, compress, tldr, bullets, etc.) currently demands a frontend deploy because the prompt strings live in TypeScript. This is a tax on the one person who pays it: Sam, the solo builder iterating on prompt quality. Every prompt tweak is a full Angular rebuild + deploy cycle, and the frontend carries 400+ lines of AI behavior knowledge it has no business knowing.

Phase 3 collapses that cost. Moving instruction logic into backend SKILL.md files means prompts iterate at the speed of editing markdown — no rebuild, no deploy, no version skew between TS and Python. The frontend shrinks to a dumb facade client (~3 lines per action), and the backend becomes the single source of truth for AI behavior. This unlocks faster prompt iteration on the actions Sam uses daily (brainstorm, rewrite, tldr) and removes the structural barrier to adding new actions.

The market here is a market of one — Sam — but the principle generalizes: every future spec-doc consumer (mobile client, OpenClaw skill, CLI) gets a clean flat API contract with zero embedded prompt knowledge, instead of inheriting the TypeScript prompt tax.

## Scope

### What This Epic Covers
- Flat action-named routes — `POST /api/text/<action>` for brainstorm, expand, compress, clarify, simplify, tldr, bullets, rewrite
- SKILL.md authoring for the 6 actions that may not have backend skills yet (expand, compress, clarify, simplify, tldr, bullets)
- Frontend `ai.service.ts` rewrite — strip all instruction strings, point at new base URL, ~3 lines per method
- Followup brainstorm consolidation — single `/api/text/brainstorm` route accepts optional `{ question, context }`; SKILL.md branches on presence
- `style` enum for `/rewrite` — Concise, Technical, Executive, Narrative, Punchy validated server-side; 400 on unknown
- Deletion sweep — remove `/api/ai/text/rewrite`, `/api/ai/text/generate`, `/api/ai/text/iterate`, `/api/ai/text/lint-braindump`, `/api/ai/text/review`, `text_prompts.py`, and dead TypeScript prompt arrays

### What This Epic Does NOT Cover
- ❌ Bootstrap-project / generate-epic-guide refactor — async multi-step, deferred to Phase 4
- ❌ `quality/` module changes — separate audit, not blocking
- ❌ `task_gen.py` refactor — still in use by active routes, separate audit
- ❌ Backwards-compatible aliasing of `/api/ai/text/rewrite` → `/api/text/rewrite` — atomic cutover; revisit only if external client surfaces
- ❌ Project CRUD, auth middleware, billing — untouched

## Tasks

| # | Task | Dependencies | Parallel | Effort | Priority |
|---|------|--------------|----------|--------|----------|
| 1 | **Author SKILL.md for missing actions** | None | Yes (with #2 scaffold) | 1 day | High |
| 2 | **Build `/api/text` blueprint with 8 thin handlers** | #1 | — | 1 day | High |
| 3 | **Rewrite `ai.service.ts` to dumb facade** | #2 | Yes (with #4 mock) | 0.5 days | High |
| 4 | **End-to-end test all 8 actions + followup brainstorm** | #2, #3 | — | 0.5 days | High |
| 5 | **Delete dead routes, `text_prompts.py`, and TS prompt strings** | #4 | — | 0.5 days | Low |

## Success Criteria

- ✅ Every text action callable as `POST /api/text/<action>` with `{ text }` (or `{ text, style }` for rewrite) returning `{ text, latencyMs }`
- ✅ Zero prompt strings, system instructions, or AI behavior comments remain in `ai.service.ts` or any frontend file
- ✅ Each Python route handler is ~10 lines: validate → call skill → return
- ✅ `style` values for `/rewrite` validated against the 5-value enum; unknown styles return 400
- ✅ Followup brainstorm flows through `/api/text/brainstorm` with `{ question, context }` — no dedicated route
- ✅ `text_prompts.py` (423 LOC) deleted; its tests deleted; no imports remain
- ✅ Old `/api/ai/text/rewrite`, `/generate`, `/iterate`, `/lint-braindump`, `/review` routes return 404
- ✅ All SKILL.md files for the 8 actions exist under `plugin/skills/` and are loaded by the skill adapter
- ✅ `ng build --configuration production` passes; backend tests green; manual smoke test of all 8 actions + followup passes

## Related Documents

- [Analysis](./analysis.md) – Problems driving this epic
- [Solution Architecture](./architecture.md) – System design
- [Timeline](./timeline.md) – Status tracking

Design the solution architecture to fulfill the tasks and scope defined above.

## CODEBASE CONTEXT (current project state — use real paths, reuse existing modules)

## Key URLs (local dev, no Docker)

| Service | URL |
|---------|-----|
| Flask API | http://localhost:5001 |
| Angular SPA | http://localhost:4201 |

## Chain Adapter

All AI calls go through `modules/runtime/chain/adapter.py` only. Never import from `providers/*` directly.

- `CHAIN_PROVIDER=cli` → subprocess `claude -p` (local dev + Docker)
- `CHAIN_AGENT=chain-agent` → routes through `claude --agent chain-agent -p`
- `CHAIN_PROVIDER=mock` → deterministic fixture output (tests only)

## Background Jobs

## Test Suite

```bash

pytest -q          # full suite

```


## REFERENCE CODE (port from, not code in the target repo)
# Reference Code — Patterns to Port

These are real working patterns from sibling projects. When architecture says "port from references.md",
describe the shape to port — not the implementation detail.

## financing-plugin — Claude Code Plugin Structure

The gold standard for a well-structured Claude Code plugin.
Location: `~/Projects/financing-plugin-extracted/`

### Plugin Layout Pattern
```
plugin-name/
├── .claude-plugin/plugin.json   # Plugin metadata + version
├── agents/                      # Specialised agents as flat .md files
├── hooks/                       # SessionStart hook (context injection)
├── references/                  # Convention references (single source of truth)
├── skills/                      # Skills — each a SKILL.md
│   ├── SKILL_MAP.md             # Master index of all skills
│   ├── feature-pipeline/SKILL.md   # Orchestrator skill
│   ├── feature-requirement/SKILL.md
│   └── dev-build/SKILL.md       # Dev tools
└── docs/                        # Spec-doc specs (Epic, Architecture)
```

Key rule: **references are the source of truth** — no rules duplicated inline in agents/skills.
Skills read from `references/*.md`, never inline the same constraint twice.

### SessionStart Hook Pattern
The hook fires on every session start and injects live context into the agent.
No heavy I/O — just read files and compute a snapshot. Fast and deterministic.

### Skill File Pattern (SKILL.md)
```markdown
# Skill Name

## When to use
[Trigger conditions]

## What I do
[Steps the agent takes]

## Tools available
[Bash, Read, Write, etc.]

## Examples
[Sample invocations]
```

## OpenClaw Workspace Files — Context Injection Pattern

The workspace files already loaded by OpenClaw every session:
- `AGENTS.md` — session instructions (auto-loaded)
- `USER.md` — who Sam is (auto-loaded)
- `MEMORY.md` — curated long-term memory (auto-loaded in main session)
- `TOOLS.md` — stack + environment (auto-loaded)

Port pattern: new skills should reference these files rather than duplicating their content.
`SOUL.md` defines agent identity — skills can refer to it for tone/style.

## spec-doc Bootstrap Adapter — Async 202 + Polling Pattern

Already shipping in spec-doc. Port this pattern for any long-running skill:
1. POST trigger → return 202 + job_id immediately
2. Background thread runs the work
3. GET /status/{job_id} polls until `done: true`
4. In-process dict keyed by project/job id — no Redis needed

Location: `~/Projects/2026/spec-doc/api/modules/ai/routes/text.py` (bootstrap)
and `~/Projects/2026/spec-doc/api/modules/ai/routes/task_gen.py` (generate-task)

## Trendfy — Docker + Deploy Pattern

gunicorn config for Flask with background threads:
```
gunicorn --bind 0.0.0.0:3101 --workers 1 --threads 4 --timeout 900 --worker-class gthread
```
`--workers 1` required when using in-process state dicts (no cross-worker sharing).
`gthread` allows daemon threads to coexist with gunicorn.

## humanize-me — Flask Thin Layer Pattern

Flask as a ~150 line AI service boundary:
- All routes: validate → call AI adapter → return streaming or JSON
- No business logic in routes
- Supabase accessed only through Flask, never from frontend directly


## CONTENT ROUTING RULES (violations are failures)
- Status words (Done, In Progress, Completed) → ONLY in timeline.md
- Code blocks with implementation → ONLY in implementation guides
- Business value and market analysis → ONLY in epic.md
- Design decisions and tech stack → ONLY in architecture.md
- Step-by-step instructions → ONLY in implementation guides
- Problem identification → ONLY in analysis.md
- Cross-references MUST be bidirectional (if A→B then B→A)
- Always use "Solution Architecture" (not just "Architecture") in cross-references
## Your ONE Job
System design, decisions, trade-offs. NO code blocks. NO status.

## Output Format
OUTPUT ONLY markdown. Start with #. No preamble.

# Thin API Phase 3 — Braindump

## What this is

Phase 3 of the thin API migration. Phase 2 added the generic skill infrastructure (SKILL.md files, generic skill route). Phase 3 is about:

1. Clean, flat, action-named API contract
2. Frontend becomes dumb — sends data, gets result, knows nothing about prompts or skills
3. All instruction complexity moves to the backend (Python route → skill → SKILL.md → Claude)
4. Dead routes and dead Python deleted

## The problem with the current frontend

`ai.service.ts` today has the brainstorm prompt instructions hardcoded in TypeScript:

```ts
brainstorm(text: string): Promise<TextOperationResponse> {
  return this.rewrite(text, [
    'You are a product thinking partner. Given this raw brain dump, generate a structured brainstorm response...',
    '1. **Key Themes** — ...',
    ...
  ].join('
'));
}
```

This is wrong. Prompt engineering in TypeScript means:
- Prompts can't be improved without a frontend deploy
- The frontend is aware of AI instructions — it shouldn't be
- All the expand/compress/clarify/simplify/tldr/bullets variants are just `rewrite()` with different instruction strings baked in TypeScript

The fix: each action gets a named flat endpoint. The backend owns the instructions. Frontend sends `{ text }` and gets `{ text, latencyMs }`.

## Current API surface (frontend perspective)

### What the frontend actually calls today

**ai.service.ts:**
- `POST /api/ai/text/rewrite` — used for rewrite, expand, compress, clarify, simplify, tldr, bullets, brainstorm, styleAs (all same endpoint, different instruction strings)
- `POST /api/ai/text/generate` — generic text generation with `{ prompt, tone }`

**projects.service.ts:**
- `POST /api/ai/text/bootstrap-project` — async spec generation (multi-step AI chain)
- `GET /api/ai/text/bootstrap-project/status/<job_id>` — poll bootstrap
- `POST /api/projects/<id>/generate-epic-guide` — async epic guide generation
- `GET /api/projects/<id>/generate-epic-guide/status` — poll epic guide
- `GET /api/projects` — list projects
- `GET /api/projects/<id>` — get project
- `POST /api/projects` — create project
- `PUT /api/projects/<id>/files/<filename>` — save file

## Target API contract — flat, action-named routes

### Text operations (new — replaces the single /rewrite endpoint)

Each action is its own route. Backend owns all prompt logic.

```
POST /api/text/brainstorm   { text }              → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/text/expand       { text }              → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/text/compress     { text }              → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/text/clarify      { text }              → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/text/simplify     { text }              → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/text/tldr         { text }              → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/text/bullets      { text }              → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/text/rewrite      { text, style }       → { text, latencyMs }
```

`style` values for `/rewrite`: Concise | Technical | Executive | Narrative | Punchy. Backend maps these to Claude instructions. Frontend doesn't know what those instructions say.

No `/generate` endpoint — it's not used for a clear business action. Remove.

### Project management (unchanged)

```
GET    /api/projects
POST   /api/projects
GET    /api/projects/<id>
PUT    /api/projects/<id>/files/<filename>
```

### Spec generation (unchanged for Phase 3)

Bootstrap-project is a complex multi-step async Python workflow. Not a Phase 3 concern. Leave the existing endpoints.

```
POST   /api/ai/text/bootstrap-project
GET    /api/ai/text/bootstrap-project/status/<job_id>
POST   /api/projects/<id>/generate-epic-guide
GET    /api/projects/<id>/generate-epic-guide/status
```

## Backend implementation

Each new `/api/text/<action>` route is a thin Python handler:
- Auth check
- Extract `text` from body (+ `style` for rewrite)
- Call the corresponding skill (which calls SKILL.md → Claude)
- Return `{ text, latencyMs }`

The skills already exist or need creating:
- `brainstorm` skill — exists in plugin/skills/
- `rewrite` skill — exists in plugin/skills/
- `expand`, `compress`, `clarify`, `simplify`, `tldr`, `bullets` — may need SKILL.md files created

The Python routes are ~10 lines each. The intelligence lives in SKILL.md.

## What gets deleted

Once the new `/api/text/<action>` routes are live and the frontend is updated:

### Dead Python routes in text.py
- `POST /api/ai/text/rewrite` — replaced by individual action routes
- `POST /api/ai/text/generate` — removed, no equivalent needed
- `POST /api/ai/text/iterate` — was never called from frontend
- `POST /api/ai/text/lint-braindump` — was never called from frontend
- `POST /api/ai/text/review` — was never called from frontend

### Dead Python files (once routes are gone)
- `api/modules/ai/services/text_prompts.py` (423 LOC) — all prompt strings
- Their test files

### Dead TypeScript
- All instruction strings in `ai.service.ts` (the brainstorm prompt array, the style instruction map, etc.)
- The `generate()` method
- The `base = '/api/ai/text'` string

## What stays

- `bootstrap-project` and `generate-epic-guide` routes (async, complex — Phase 4)
- `quality/` module (still in use by active routes — audit separately)
- `task_gen.py` service (still in use by active routes — audit separately)
- All auth, billing, project CRUD

## What the Angular service looks like after

```typescript
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class AiService {
  private readonly base = '/api/text';
  constructor(private http: HttpClient) {}

  brainstorm(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('brainstorm', { text });
  }
  expand(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('expand', { text });
  }
  compress(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('compress', { text });
  }
  clarify(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('clarify', { text });
  }
  simplify(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('simplify', { text });
  }
  tldr(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('tldr', { text });
  }
  bullets(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('bullets', { text });
  }
  rewrite(text: string, style: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('rewrite', { text, style });
  }

  private post(action: string, body: object): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return firstValueFrom(
      this.http.post<TextResponse>(`${this.base}/${action}`, body)
        .pipe(timeout(AI_TIMEOUT_MS))
    );
  }
}
```

No instruction strings. No prompt logic. Each method is ~3 lines.

The `followupBrainstorm()` method in `app.component.ts` currently assembles context and sends a custom rewrite instruction. After Phase 3, this becomes a call to a dedicated `POST /api/text/brainstorm-followup` route, or the brainstorm skill handles the follow-up via the same `/api/text/brainstorm` endpoint with additional context in the body.

## Architectural principle — facade

The API is a facade. The frontend:
- Has zero instruction strings
- Has zero system prompts
- Has zero AI behavior knowledge
- Sends data, receives results

Every AI decision — what the prompt says, how Claude should respond, what context to include — lives in the backend. SKILL.md is the source of truth. Python routes are the facade surface.

This also resolves the followup brainstorm pattern. Currently `app.component.ts` assembles:
```ts
`You are a brainstorming partner. The user wants to explore: "${question}"
...`
```
That instruction string is eliminated. The endpoint becomes:
```
POST /api/text/brainstorm  { text, question?, context? }  → { text, latencyMs }
```
The SKILL.md decides what to do when `question` is present vs. absent. Frontend sends the data structure, knows nothing about what happens next.

Same principle for style/rewrite: frontend sends `{ text, style: "Concise" }`. Backend maps "Concise" to Claude instructions. Frontend doesn't know what "Concise" means to Claude.

## Sequence

1. Create SKILL.md files for expand, compress, clarify, simplify, tldr, bullets (if they don't exist)
2. Add Python blueprint `/api/text` with 8 route handlers (thin, call skills)
3. Update `ai.service.ts` — new base URL, clean methods, no instruction strings
4. Test end-to-end
5. Delete old `/api/ai/text/rewrite`, `/api/ai/text/generate` routes
6. Delete `text_prompts.py` and its tests
7. Delete dead TypeScript

Focus on WHY. Explain trade-offs. No code blocks.

# Engineering Principles — Sam's Projects

Non-negotiable across all projects. When a brain dump contradicts a principle, the analysis step must flag it.

## P1 — Adapter Boundary
All external service calls (AI, DB, storage, HTTP) go through a single adapter module.
No feature code imports a provider directly. The adapter is the only file that knows which provider is active.
- spec-doc: `modules/chain/adapter.py`
- OpenClaw plugins: wrap external calls in a dedicated skill or tool wrapper

## P2 — Thin HTTP Layer
Route handlers contain no business logic. Handlers: validate input → call service → return response.
- Flask: `routes.py` handles HTTP only; `service.py` holds pure Python logic
- OpenClaw: skill files describe tool invocations; no inline logic

## P3 — Async 202 + Polling for Long Operations
Any operation > 30s returns 202 immediately with a job identifier.
A background thread does the work. A status endpoint lets the client poll until `done: true`.
No HTTP connection held open. No Redis — in-process state keyed by job/project id.

## P4 — No Speculative Abstractions
Build for the one concrete case that exists now. No generic runners for one consumer.
No base classes for one subclass. No registries for one item.
Three similar lines of code is better than a premature abstraction.

## P5 — OpenAPI-First (spec-doc)
`openapi.yaml` is the contract. DTOs are generated from it. Never hand-edit generated files.
Routes implement the contract — not the other way around.

## P6 — OpenClaw Plugin Principles
- Skills first: start with `SKILL.md` files (no build step, iterate fast)
- Graduate to `openclaw.plugin.json` package only when skills hit real limits
- References are the single source of truth — no rules duplicated inline in agents/skills
- Agents are declarative descriptions, not imperative code
- Context files (`MEMORY.md`, `USER.md`, `TOOLS.md`) are loaded every session — keep them current
- Boot hooks fire on session start — keep them cheap (no blocking I/O)
- Channel-aware: skills must adjust output format per channel (Telegram ≠ web UI)

## P7 — File Size & Structure
- Files under 200 lines (hard target, not a guideline)
- Named exports only (no default exports in Angular/TS)
- One component per file
- Build verification required before each commit (Angular: `ng build --configuration production`)

## Code Rules
- No direct push to master — always PRs; PRs target master; live is deploy branch
- Daemon threads only (`daemon=True`) — never block server shutdown
- Empty context strings handled gracefully — callers never crash on missing context
- `read_context()` returns `""` for missing files; `PromptBuilder.section()` skips empty content

# 🎯 Epic: Thin API Phase 3

## Business Value

Spec-doc's text-action AI features are growing fast — every new variant (expand, compress, tldr, bullets, etc.) currently demands a frontend deploy because the prompt strings live in TypeScript. # Thin API Phase 3 — Braindump

## What this is

Phase 3 of the thin API migration. Phase 2 added the generic skill infrastructure (SKILL.md files, generic skill route). Phase 3 is about:

1. Clean, flat, action-named API contract
2. Frontend becomes dumb — sends data, gets result, knows nothing about prompts or skills
3. All instruction complexity moves to the backend (Python route → skill → SKILL.md → Claude)
4. Dead routes and dead Python deleted

## The problem with the current frontend

`ai.service.ts` today has the brainstorm prompt instructions hardcoded in TypeScript:

```ts
brainstorm(text: string): Promise<TextOperationResponse> {
  return this.rewrite(text, [
    'You are a product thinking partner. Given this raw brain dump, generate a structured brainstorm response...',
    '1. **Key Themes** — ...',
    ...
  ].join('
'));
}
```

This is wrong. Prompt engineering in TypeScript means:
- Prompts can't be improved without a frontend deploy
- The frontend is aware of AI instructions — it shouldn't be
- All the expand/compress/clarify/simplify/tldr/bullets variants are just `rewrite()` with different instruction strings baked in TypeScript

The fix: each action gets a named flat endpoint. The backend owns the instructions. Frontend sends `{ text }` and gets `{ text, latencyMs }`.

## Current API surface (frontend perspective)

### What the frontend actually calls today

**ai.service.ts:**
- `POST /api/ai/text/rewrite` — used for rewrite, expand, compress, clarify, simplify, tldr, bullets, brainstorm, styleAs (all same endpoint, different instruction strings)
- `POST /api/ai/text/generate` — generic text generation with `{ prompt, tone }`

**projects.service.ts:**
- `POST /api/ai/text/bootstrap-project` — async spec generation (multi-step AI chain)
- `GET /api/ai/text/bootstrap-project/status/<job_id>` — poll bootstrap
- `POST /api/projects/<id>/generate-epic-guide` — async epic guide generation
- `GET /api/projects/<id>/generate-epic-guide/status` — poll epic guide
- `GET /api/projects` — list projects
- `GET /api/projects/<id>` — get project
- `POST /api/projects` — create project
- `PUT /api/projects/<id>/files/<filename>` — save file

## Target API contract — flat, action-named routes

### Text operations (new — replaces the single /rewrite endpoint)

Each action is its own route. Backend owns all prompt logic.

```
POST /api/text/brainstorm   { text }              → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/text/expand       { text }              → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/text/compress     { text }              → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/text/clarify      { text }              → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/text/simplify     { text }              → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/text/tldr         { text }              → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/text/bullets      { text }              → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/text/rewrite      { text, style }       → { text, latencyMs }
```

`style` values for `/rewrite`: Concise | Technical | Executive | Narrative | Punchy. Backend maps these to Claude instructions. Frontend doesn't know what those instructions say.

No `/generate` endpoint — it's not used for a clear business action. Remove.

### Project management (unchanged)

```
GET    /api/projects
POST   /api/projects
GET    /api/projects/<id>
PUT    /api/projects/<id>/files/<filename>
```

### Spec generation (unchanged for Phase 3)

Bootstrap-project is a complex multi-step async Python workflow. Not a Phase 3 concern. Leave the existing endpoints.

```
POST   /api/ai/text/bootstrap-project
GET    /api/ai/text/bootstrap-project/status/<job_id>
POST   /api/projects/<id>/generate-epic-guide
GET    /api/projects/<id>/generate-epic-guide/status
```

## Backend implementation

Each new `/api/text/<action>` route is a thin Python handler:
- Auth check
- Extract `text` from body (+ `style` for rewrite)
- Call the corresponding skill (which calls SKILL.md → Claude)
- Return `{ text, latencyMs }`

- `brainstorm` skill — exists in plugin/skills/

- `expand`, `compress`, `clarify`, `simplify`, `tldr`, `bullets` — may need SKILL.md files created

The Python routes are ~10 lines each. The intelligence lives in SKILL.md.

## What gets deleted

Once the new `/api/text/<action>` routes are live and the frontend is updated:

### Dead Python routes in text.py
- `POST /api/ai/text/rewrite` — replaced by individual action routes
- `POST /api/ai/text/generate` — removed, no equivalent needed
- `POST /api/ai/text/iterate` — was never called from frontend
- `POST /api/ai/text/lint-braindump` — was never called from frontend

### Dead Python files (once routes are gone)
- `api/modules/ai/services/text_prompts.py` (423 LOC) — all prompt strings
- Their test files

### Dead TypeScript
- All instruction strings in `ai.service.ts` (the brainstorm prompt array, the style instruction map, etc.)
- The `generate()` method
- The `base = '/api/ai/text'` string

## What stays

- `bootstrap-project` and `generate-epic-guide` routes (async, complex — Phase 4)
- `quality/` module (still in use by active routes — audit separately)
- `task_gen.py` service (still in use by active routes — audit separately)
- All auth, billing, project CRUD

## What the Angular service looks like after

```typescript
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class AiService {
  private readonly base = '/api/text';
  constructor(private http: HttpClient) {}

  brainstorm(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('brainstorm', { text });
  }
  expand(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('expand', { text });
  }
  compress(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('compress', { text });
  }
  clarify(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('clarify', { text });
  }
  simplify(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('simplify', { text });
  }
  tldr(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('tldr', { text });
  }
  bullets(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('bullets', { text });
  }
  rewrite(text: string, style: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('rewrite', { text, style });
  }

  private post(action: string, body: object): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return firstValueFrom(
      this.http.post<TextResponse>(`${this.base}/${action}`, body)
        .pipe(timeout(AI_TIMEOUT_MS))
    );
  }
}
```

No instruction strings. No prompt logic. Each method is ~3 lines.

The `followupBrainstorm()` method in `app.component.ts` currently assembles context and sends a custom rewrite instruction. After Phase 3, this becomes a call to a dedicated `POST /api/text/brainstorm-followup` route, or the brainstorm skill handles the follow-up via the same `/api/text/brainstorm` endpoint with additional context in the body.

## Architectural principle — facade

The API is a facade. The frontend:
- Has zero instruction strings
- Has zero system prompts
- Has zero AI behavior knowledge
- Sends data, receives results

Every AI decision — what the prompt says, how Claude should respond, what context to include — lives in the backend. SKILL.md is the source of truth. Python routes are the facade surface.

This also resolves the followup brainstorm pattern. Currently `app.component.ts` assembles:
```ts
`You are a brainstorming partner. The user wants to explore: "${question}"
...`
```
That instruction string is eliminated. The endpoint becomes:
```
POST /api/text/brainstorm  { text, question?, context? }  → { text, latencyMs }
```
The SKILL.md decides what to do when `question` is present vs. absent. Frontend sends the data structure, knows nothing about what happens next.

Same principle for style/rewrite: frontend sends `{ text, style: "Concise" }`. Backend maps "Concise" to Claude instructions. Frontend doesn't know what "Concise" means to Claude.

## Sequence

1. Create SKILL.md files for expand, compress, clarify, simplify, tldr, bullets (if they don't exist)
2. Add Python blueprint `/api/text` with 8 route handlers (thin, call skills)
3. Update `ai.service.ts` — new base URL, clean methods, no instruction strings
4. Test end-to-end
5. Delete old `/api/ai/text/rewrite`, `/api/ai/text/generate` routes
6. Delete `text_prompts.py` and its tests
7. Delete dead TypeScript

# 🏗️ Solution Architecture: Thin API Phase 3

## Architecture Overview

Phase 3 reshapes the text-action surface around a single architectural insight: **the frontend should not be a participant in prompt engineering**. Today, `ai.service.ts` carries instruction strings, role descriptions, and behavior contracts that belong to the AI layer — and every prompt tweak forces an Angular rebuild. The fix is to invert the contract: the frontend becomes a **dumb facade client** that sends typed data and receives typed results, while the backend becomes the **single source of truth** for all AI behavior, with SKILL.md files holding the authoritative instructions.

The mental model is a three-layer collapse: HTTP (action-named flat routes) → Skill (SKILL.md owns instructions) → Chain Adapter (the only AI-call boundary). Each `/api/text/<action>` route is a ~10-line handler whose only job is to validate input and dispatch to the right skill. The skill resolves to a SKILL.md, which Claude reads at execution time. This means a prompt change is a markdown edit, not a deploy. New actions are a new SKILL.md plus a new route handler — no frontend involvement.

The cutover is **atomic, not aliased**. There is no period where both `/api/ai/text/rewrite` and `/api/text/rewrite` coexist. Phase 2 already laid the generic skill route and SKILL.md infrastructure; Phase 3 simply names eight specific actions on top of it and removes the legacy surface in the same release. This is appropriate because spec-doc has a market of one — Sam — so backwards-compatible aliasing buys nothing and adds drift risk.

## Design Principles

| Principle | Application |
|-----------|-------------|
| P1 — Adapter Boundary | Routes never touch a provider; they call skills, which call the existing `runtime/chain/adapter.py`. The adapter remains the single AI-call boundary. |
| P2 — Thin HTTP Layer | Every `/api/text/<action>` handler is validate → dispatch skill → return. No prompt assembly, no business logic, no provider awareness in the route file. |
| P4 — No Speculative Abstractions | Eight named handlers, eight named methods on the Angular service. No generic action registry, no metaclass-driven dispatcher, no plugin loader for one consumer. |
| P6 — OpenClaw Plugin Principles | SKILL.md files are authoritative; rules live in references, not duplicated inline. New skills (expand, compress, etc.) follow the existing plugin/skills/ shape. |
| P7 — File Size & Structure | The new `routes/text.py` blueprint stays well under 200 lines (eight 10-line handlers + small helpers). `ai.service.ts` shrinks from ~400+ lines to ~50. |
| Facade Asymmetry | The frontend knows action names; the backend knows behavior. The `style` enum is the only structured argument that crosses the wire — its meaning is opaque to the client. |

## Component Design

### `/api/text` Blueprint (Backend Facade)

**Purpose**: Expose eight action-named routes that map 1:1 to user-facing text operations. Each route is a thin Flask handler that validates inputs, invokes the matching skill, and returns `{ text, latencyMs }`.

**Boundaries**: Owns HTTP concerns (auth, body parsing, status codes, timing). Does not own prompts, does not own provider selection, does not assemble instructions. The handler for `/rewrite` validates `style` against the five-value enum and rejects unknowns with 400 — that's the only branching logic any route contains.

**Why eight handlers, not one parameterized route**: A single `/api/text/<action>` with dynamic dispatch would be smaller, but it shifts validation into a runtime registry and obscures the contract. Eight named handlers make the API surface inspectable from the route file, give each action its own auth/error boundary, and align with P4 — there is no second consumer that would benefit from a generic dispatcher.

### Skill Resolution Layer

**Purpose**: Bridge between Python route handlers and SKILL.md files. Each action name resolves to a skill identifier; the skill adapter loads the SKILL.md, injects the request payload as context, and routes through the chain adapter.

**Boundaries**: This already exists from Phase 2 (generic skill route). Phase 3 reuses it — no new infrastructure. The new actions (expand, compress, clarify, simplify, tldr, bullets) are added as SKILL.md files in `plugin/skills/`; brainstorm and rewrite skills already exist.

**Why reuse, not rebuild**: Phase 2 already paid the abstraction cost. Phase 3's job is to put a clean facade in front of it, not introduce a parallel mechanism.

### Brainstorm Skill (Bimodal)

**Purpose**: Handle both standalone brainstorm (`{ text }`) and followup brainstorm (`{ text, question, context }`) through a single endpoint and a single SKILL.md.

**Why one endpoint, not two**: A separate `/brainstorm-followup` route would mean two SKILL.md files that share 80% of their behavior — a maintenance hazard. The skill itself is well-suited to branch on payload shape because branching on input is exactly what natural language instructions handle gracefully. The frontend submits a structured payload; the SKILL.md decides how to use the optional fields.

**Trade-off accepted**: One skill carries two modes, which is mildly less explicit than two skills. We accept this because the alternative duplicates the brainstorm voice and instructions across two markdown files, and drift between them is a real risk.

### `style` Enum for Rewrite

**Purpose**: The single piece of behavior-shaping data that crosses the API boundary. Five named styles (Concise, Technical, Executive, Narrative, Punchy) are the contract; the frontend sends a name, the backend maps it.

**Why server-validated, not free-form**: Allowing arbitrary style strings from the client would re-open the prompt-injection-from-the-frontend problem we're closing. The enum is the firewall: unknown values return 400, the SKILL.md resolves known values to instructions. The frontend learns no more about "Concise" than the user does about how Claude was prompted.

**Trade-off accepted**: Adding a sixth style requires a backend change. This is correct — style additions are AI-behavior decisions and belong in the backend, not the client.

### `ai.service.ts` (Frontend Facade Client)

**Purpose**: Eight typed methods, each ~3 lines, plus a single private `post()` helper. Zero instruction strings, zero prompt arrays, zero awareness of Claude.

**Boundaries**: HTTP transport only. Method names mirror route names. The signature differences (`rewrite(text, style)` vs the others taking just `text`) are the only contract surface; everything else is symmetrical.

**Why named methods, not a single `call(action, payload)`**: Type safety and discoverability. Each method's signature is the contract for that action. A single dispatch method would push action-name validation to runtime and weaken IDE autocomplete — the kinds of speculative abstraction P4 forbids.

### Deletion Sweep

**Purpose**: Remove the legacy surface in the same release as the new one ships. This is not housekeeping — it's load-bearing for the architectural claim. As long as `text_prompts.py` and TypeScript prompt arrays exist, two sources of truth exist, and the facade promise is hollow.

**Scope**: Five legacy routes (`/rewrite`, `/generate`, `/iterate`, `/lint-braindump`, `/review`), `text_prompts.py` (423 LOC) and its tests, all instruction-bearing TypeScript in `ai.service.ts`, and the `base = '/api/ai/text'` constant. Out of scope by design: bootstrap-project, generate-epic-guide, `quality/`, `task_gen.py` — these are still in active use and belong to a separate audit.

## Technology Stack

| Layer | Choice | Rationale |
|-------|--------|-----------|
| Frontend | Angular 17 standalone + signals + HttpClient | Existing stack; Phase 3 simplifies what's there, doesn't change the platform. |
| HTTP Layer | Flask Blueprint at `/api/text` | Matches `routes/text.py` pattern already used elsewhere; thin-handler convention is established. |
| Auth | `require_auth` decorator on every route | Reuse existing JWT middleware; no new auth concerns introduced. |
| Skill Layer | Phase 2's generic skill adapter + SKILL.md files in `plugin/skills/` | Already shipping; Phase 3 adds six SKILL.md files, no new code paths. |
| AI Boundary | `runtime/chain/adapter.py` (unchanged) | The only AI call boundary. Skills route through it; routes never touch it directly. |
| Validation | Inline Python checks (text presence, style enum) | Eight routes don't justify a schema framework; explicit checks fit the thin-handler shape. |

## Design Decisions

| Decision | Rationale | Trade-offs |
|----------|-----------|------------|
| Atomic cutover, no aliasing of `/api/ai/text/*` → `/api/text/*` | Single consumer (Sam's frontend); aliases cost drift risk and zero readability. The deletion sweep is the architectural payload — keeping legacy routes around defeats the facade claim. | If an unknown external client surfaces, it breaks. Acceptable: spec-doc has no external API consumers, and the route names are flat enough that reintroducing an alias later is a 2-line patch. |
| Eight named handlers + eight named Angular methods, not parameterized dispatch | Explicit contract, type safety, P4 compliance. The eight actions are the concrete cases that exist now — no ninth lurking. | Adding a ninth action means two new lines (route + method) in two files. Trivial cost. |
| Single `/brainstorm` route handles followup via optional `{ question, context }` | One skill, one endpoint, one place to evolve brainstorm voice. SKILL.md handles natural-language branching better than Python control flow. | Slightly less explicit than two routes. Acceptable because the alternative duplicates instruction content across SKILL.md files. |
| `style` is a server-validated enum, not a free-form instruction string | Keeps prompt content out of the client; closes the path that today lets `app.component.ts` assemble instruction strings. | Adding a style requires a backend change. This is the right place for that change to live. |
| Reuse Phase 2's skill adapter; no new orchestration layer | Phase 2 already paid the cost. Phase 3 is facade + cleanup, not new infrastructure. | None — we'd be re-implementing what already works. |
| Delete `text_prompts.py` and its tests in the same release as the new routes ship | Two sources of truth is the problem we're solving; leaving the old one around defeats the migration. | Forces ordering: SKILL.md files must be authored and verified before deletion. The Epic sequences this correctly (deletion is the last task). |
| Keep bootstrap-project and generate-epic-guide on the legacy `/api/ai/text/*` surface | Async multi-step chains have different shape (202 + polling) from synchronous text actions. Mixing them under `/api/text` would confuse the contract. Phase 4 will handle them separately. | The codebase carries two URL prefixes for a release cycle. Acceptable — the prefixes encode a real semantic difference (sync vs async), so the inconsistency is informative. |
| No streaming for Phase 3 actions | All eight actions are short single-shot transforms; latency is bounded by Claude response time. Streaming adds client-side complexity (SSE handling) for no perceived UX gain on these payloads. | If a future action benefits from streaming, it gets its own route with `stream_generate` from the adapter. P4-compliant: don't build it until needed. |
| Backend returns `{ text, latencyMs }` (not just `text`) | `latencyMs` is already in the existing response shape; preserving it keeps the frontend's existing latency telemetry working without a parallel migration. | Trivially small overhead in the response. Worth it to avoid coupled changes. |

## Related Documents

- [Analysis](./analysis.md) – Problems driving design
- [Epic](./epic.md) – Scope and tasks
- [Timeline](./timeline.md) – Status tracking
